items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: But he had a knack of five or six women's at a dance with Jack Kerrin in. Playing at National Park.

ctx.x: Well, I guess a lot of people used to do all kind of things in those days.

Boysmen. Well, we had a guitar player. I'll forget that boy's name. But he had a knack of five or six women's at a dance with Jack Kerrin in. Playing at National Park. Boy, that was a jumping spot. And he danced five and six girls there. And he's bigoted like, you know. He's nice looking, but he's bigoted. I can't call his name. You go ahead, I'll see you tomorrow. You go ahead, I'll see you. And all that. Kept on with that stuff. But one of them guys, I pardoned him. He sold up like that. Don't nobody know what…
They said that about Buddy Bolden, too.
